audit.whatIsWrong: The entry is built around an ability called "Repeating Dashes", which Ambessa does not have, and it describes her W as a dash-chain.
audit.why: Her real abilities are Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E) and Public Execution (R). Drakehound's Step is the dash: entering a move or attack command while casting an ability makes her dash and empowers the next attack. Repudiation is the opposite of mobility — an 18/17/16/15/14s brace that shields her and slams, hitting harder if it absorbed non-minion damage, which is exactly what eats a raw Crushing Blow.
audit.corrected: "Repeating Dashes" replaced with Drakehound's Step throughout the writable text; spikes[0].text rewritten to name the real dash and to stop calling Repudiation a dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows contradicted their own whys[] line — win[1] and win[2] said Ambessa where the whys say "stays a skill matchup" and "remains even"; win[3] said Skill where the why says your window out-trades her; win[4] said Skill where the why says her R wins the all-in; win[6] said Ambessa where the why says late evens out.
audit.why: The packet levelChart is Skill / Skill / Skill / Wukong / Ambessa / Ambessa / Skill, which matches the prose line for line and matches the mechanics: even until 4, your burst window at 4-5, then Public Execution at 6.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described with no numbers and no mechanic — just "a long dash-lockdown ult that out-ranges your engage".
audit.why: Public Execution is 130/115/100s and it blinks to the FARTHEST enemy champion in a line she chooses, suppresses on arrival, then slams and stuns. Which champion it grabs is a positioning decision, and a 130s rank-1 cooldown is a whole wave of freedom once she misses it.
audit.corrected: 130s and the farthest-target-in-line mechanic written into spikes[1].text and phases[4].why.
